## Cosmic accelerators and their messengers {#cosmic-messengers}

Charged cosmic rays bend in magnetic fields.

Photons can scatter or be absorbed.

Neutrinos can escape dense environments and preserve directional information.

::: {.notes}
Source physics occupies 20–30 minutes. State the energy range and avoid
suggesting unlimited neutrino transparency at every energy and column depth.

Source: [D'Ammando, AGN review](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.30764).
:::

## Acceleration and confinement {#acceleration-and-confinement}

$$
r_L=\frac{p}{ZeB}\lesssim R
$$

A source must retain particles long enough to accelerate them.

Energy losses and the available time also limit the maximum energy.

::: {.notes}
The displayed gyroradius uses SI units for momentum, magnetic field and charge.
The confinement condition is necessary, but not sufficient for acceleration.
Use a Hillas diagram with explicit units when developing this slide.
:::

## Making pions, making neutrinos {#pion-production}

$$
pp\ \text{or}\ p\gamma\ \longrightarrow\ \pi^{\pm},\pi^0+X
$$
$$
\pi^+\to\mu^++\nu_\mu,
\qquad\mu^+\to e^++\nu_e+\bar\nu_\mu,
\qquad\pi^0\to\gamma\gamma.
$$

::: {.notes}
The schematic first line combines processes with different thresholds and
branching fractions. Explain matter and radiation targets separately.

Source: [D'Ammando, production mechanisms](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.30764).
:::

## What neutrino energy tells us {#parent-particle-energy}

$$
E_\nu\sim0.05E_p
$$

A useful scale estimate for pion production and decay.

The detailed relation depends on the interaction and the source conditions.

::: {.notes}
Present this as an approximate energy partition, not a universal event-level
conversion. Cooling and spectra change the neutrino yield.

Source: [Spiering, section 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26436).
:::

<!-- Visual slot: energy partition, without a false precision claim. -->

## Candidate source populations {#source-populations}

- Galactic accelerators and interactions with interstellar gas.
- Active galactic nuclei: jets and compact central regions.
- Star-forming environments.
- Transients, including gamma-ray bursts and tidal disruption events.

::: {.notes}
Distinguish proposed production sites, observed associations and established
diffuse components. Avoid implying that every class has a detected neutrino
signal.

Sources: [D'Ammando](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.30764) and
[Spiering, sections 5–6](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26436).
:::

## Hidden neutrino sources {#hidden-sources}

Gamma rays can lose energy inside the source while neutrinos escape.

$$
\gamma+\gamma\longrightarrow e^++e^-.
$$

::: {.question}
Could a bright neutrino source be faint in high-energy gamma rays?
:::

::: {.notes}
Introduce electromagnetic reprocessing and its observational constraints.
Use the AGN disk/corona as a model example, not a uniquely established
location of neutrino production.

Source: [D'Ammando, NGC 1068 models](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.30764).
:::
